{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_bdrk_015FE96mEBX3FjMto2FoKwpL","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Eval harness — rubric, test prompts, protocol\n2\t\n3\tMeasures whether a produced BUILD PLAN actually follows the skill. Score is **/20**:\n4\t10 dimensions, 0–2 points each.\n5\t\n6\t## Rubric (0–2 per dimension)\n7\t\n8\tScoring per dimension: **0** = absent, **1** = present but weak/partial, **2** = done well.\n9\t\n10\t1. **Dependency ordering** — phases go substrate → upward; nothing specified before its\n11\t   dependency is proven.\n12\t2. **Walking skeleton first** — a real end-to-end prod path is Phase 0, before features.\n13\t3. **Tradeoff gates up front** — irreversible decisions listed with default + flip condition,\n14\t   no silent assumptions.\n15\t4. **Blast-radius ordering within phases** — widest-impact work precedes leaf work.\n16\t5. **Security threaded every phase** — not a trailing step.\n17\t6. **Observability from day zero** — present in Phase 0 and every phase after.\n18\t7. **Reproducibility threaded** — builds/data/envs are reproducible across phases.\n19\t8. **Resilience threaded** — failure handling appears across phases, not only at the end.\n20\t9. **AI layer correctness** (AI systems) — defenses+budgets+HITL before capabilities, then\n21\t   retrieval → model access → memory → orchestration → routing → feedback.\n22\t   *(Non-AI systems: award 2 if the plan correctly declares the AI layer N/A.)*\n23\t10. **Deferred work made explicit** — what's not built yet, with a pull-forward condition.\n24\t\n25\t**Thresholds:** >=16 ship. 12–15 revise the weak dimensions. <12 re-plan from Step 1.\n26\t\n27\t## Fixed test prompts\n28\t\n29\tRun the skill against each; score with the rubric.\n30\t\n31\t- **P1 (AI):** \"Plan a customer-support RAG chatbot over our help-center docs.\"\n32\t- **P2 (software):** \"Architect a multi-tenant SaaS billing system.\"\n33\t- **P3 (infra):** \"Sequence building a CI/CD platform for 50 microservices.\"\n34\t- **P4 (AI-agentic):** \"Plan an autonomous agent that triages and resolves GitHub issues.\"\n35\t- **P5 (software):** \"Order the build of a real-time collaborative document editor.\"\n36\t\n37\t## Protocol\n38\t\n39\t1. Run the plan generator (with the skill) on a prompt.\n40\t2. Score each of the 10 dimensions 0–2; sum to /20.\n41\t3. Record the score and the weakest dimension.\n42\t\n43\t## With-skill vs without-skill baseline\n44\t\n45\tFor the same prompt, compare:\n46\t- **Without skill:** a plan written feature-first / by visibility. Walking skeleton (Phase 0)\n**The one real request:** `exifrename ./fixtures/one --apply` on a folder with **one real JPEG** that has `DateTimeOriginal`.\n**The real response:** `IMG_0412.JPG` becomes `2024-06-01_14-32-05.JPG`. Each aborts cleanly with a reason code.\n  4. **A FAT/exFAT path.** These systems have no hard links (common on SD cards). Then add an `exiftool` subprocess backend (`-json -n`, batch mode) behind the same interface. |\n| **Language / distribution** | **Python 3.11+, installed with `pipx`.** Pinned `uv.lock`. Only standard-library `argparse` besides `exifread`. | Non-technical users need zero-install. Then ship PyInstaller or Nuitka single binaries. If startup time or binary size is unacceptable, rewrite the core in Go. That is expensive, so it needs evidence first. |\n| **Filename contract** (irreversible once users' libraries carry it) | `YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS<ext>`. Same-second collisions get `_01`, `_02` and so on. The original extension is **kept exactly as is**. No colons, because they are illegal on Windows. | Repeated user requests for other layouts. Then add a `--format` template. The default never changes after 1.0. |\n| **Which timestamp counts as \"capture date\"** | Use `DateTimeOriginal`, then `CreateDate`/`DateTimeDigitized`, then **missing**. `ModifyDate` is never used by default, because edits change it. | Specific camera models are shown to write only `DateTime`. Then allow `--allow-modify-date` as an opt-in. |\n| **Timezone** | Use the **wall-clock time as recorded**, with no conversion. `OffsetTimeOriginal` is logged but ignored. | Multi-timezone trip users need one consistent order. Then add `--to-utc` or `--tz`, which needs `OffsetTime*` or a user-supplied offset. |\n| **Missing EXIF fallback** | **Skip and report.** File mtime is never silently used. It is unreliable after copying. | Explicit demand. Then add `--fallback=mtime`, opt-in, with every such file flagged in the output. |\n| **Default mode** | **Dry run by default.** Changing files needs `--apply`. | None planned. This is a safety invariant. |\n| **In-place vs copy** | **In-place rename**, which is what was asked, made reversible by a journal. | Users on unreliable media (SD cards, flaky NAS) report failed runs. Then add `--copy-to DIR`. |\n| (AI) prompt+RAG vs fine-tune | N/A: no model in the system. | — |\n| (AI) hosted API vs self-host | N/A: no model. **Privacy boundary still applies:** photo metadata (GPS, device serial numbers) never leaves the machine. | — |\n\n## 3. Walking skeleton (Phase 0)\n**The one real request:** `exifrename ./fixtures/one --apply` on a folder with **one real JPEG** that has `DateTimeOriginal`.\n**The real response:** `IMG_0412.JPG` becomes `2024-06-01_14-32-05.JPG`. One JSON log line, a summary line (`renamed=1 skipped=0 failed=0`), and exit code `0`.\n\n**Tiers crossed (each the thinnest version that works):**\n1. **CLI:** `argparse` reads `DIR` and `--apply`.\n2. **Scan:** non-recursive `os.scandir`, regular files only, symlinks not followed.\n3. **Extract:** `exifread` reads `DateTimeOriginal`. Missing means skip.\n4. **Plan:** compute the target name. If the target exists and is not the source, skip it with reason `collision`. No suffixing yet.\n5. **Journal:** before renaming, append `{src, dst, state}` to `.exifrename-journal-<ts>.jsonl` in the folder.\n6. **Apply:** a no-overwrite rename. On POSIX that is `os.link` + `os.unlink` where hard links work; otherwise an exists-check + `os.rename`. On Windows `os.rename` already refuses to overwrite.\n7. **Report:** log line, summary and exit code.\n\n**Deployed:** a GitHub Actions matrix (ubuntu, macos, windows) builds the wheel from `uv.lock`, installs it with `pipx`, and runs the command above on the committed fixture. It then asserts the new filename exists and the old one is gone. A tag push publishes to PyPI via trusted publishing.\n**Logged:** `--log-json` writes one structured line per file to stderr (`src`, `dst`, `tag_used`, `action`, `reason`). The human summary goes to stdout.\n**Monitored:** exit codes are a contract from day zero: `0` OK, `1` some files skipped, `2` usage error, `3` run aborted. The CI smoke run on every commit is the canary. There is no telemetry.\n\n**Exit check:** the released wheel, installed fresh on all three OSes, renames the real fixture JPEG. The JSON log line and the summary counts appear, and the exit code is `0`.\n\n## 4. Phases (ordered by dependency; within a phase, widest blast radius first)\n\n### Phase 0: Walking skeleton\n- **Unlocks:** every later phase. There is now a real end-to-end path to harden.\n- **Depends on:** nothing.\n- **Tasks:** (1) repo, `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, CI matrix → (2) the exit-code and log-line contract → (3) the skeleton path above → (4) publish 0.0.1.\n- **Exit check:** as in §3.\n\n### Phase 1: Date-extraction substrate (proving the thing every rename rests on)\n- **Unlocks:** trusting any computed name. Nothing about naming or collisions gets specified until this is proven.\n- **Depends on:** Phase 0's extractor slot, CLI and CI.\n- **Tasks (widest first):**\n  1. **A typed extraction result:** `Found(dt, subsec, tag, offset) | Missing | Invalid(reason)`. Every later layer consumes this, so it gets fixed first.\n  2. **A golden fixture corpus.** EXIF is written deterministically by a script (`piexif` for JPEG), plus a few small real camera files. It covers: JPEG, HEIC, DNG/CR2/NEF, PNG with no EXIF, the zero date `0000:00:00 00:00:00`, a malformed or truncated EXIF block, only `CreateDate` present, `SubSecTimeOriginal`, and `OffsetTimeOriginal`.\n  3. **Tag precedence and date validation:** reject impossible dates and years before 1990 or in the future, flagged as `Invalid`, not renamed.\n  4. **Hostile-input limits:** cap bytes read per file, set a per-file timeout, and catch every parser exception so one bad file can't crash the run.\n  5. **`--explain FILE`:** prints the tags found and which one won.\n- **Exit check:** 100% of fixtures match their expected results on all three OSes. **This is where the build-vs-buy gate is decided:** any wrong or unreadable fixture triggers the `exiftool` backend before Phase 2 begins.\n\n### Phase 2: Rename plan and safety engine (the name contract, collisions, reversibility)\n- **Unlocks:** safe `--apply` on real libraries.\n- **Depends on:** Phase 1's proven extraction result.\n- **Tasks (widest first):**\n  1. **Freeze the data contracts.** Filename format v1, the plan record (`src, dst, status, reason`), and the journal schema with a `schema_version`. Undo has to read journals written by older versions, so this has the widest blast radius in the tool.\n  2. **A deterministic plan builder.** Sort by `(datetime, subsec, original name)` so the same input always gives the same output. Same-second bursts get `_01`, `_02` in capture order.\n  3. **Collision resolution against three sets:** files already on disk, other targets in the same batch, and sources not yet renamed (chain and swap cases). On Windows and macOS, comparisons ignore case.\n  4. **Idempotency.** A file already named correctly is a no-op, so a second run reports `renamed=0`.\n  5. **`exifrename undo <journal>`** reverses completed entries in reverse order and refuses to overwrite anything.\n  6. **Dry-run output:** a readable `old → new` table, the default when `--apply` is absent.\n- **Exit check:** property tests (`hypothesis`) over random sets of names and dates show that applying the plan never loses or overwrites a file (file count and content hashes unchanged), and that `apply` then `undo` restores the original names exactly. A real folder of 1,000 or more photos runs end to end with no collisions lost.\n\n### Phase 3: Failure-safe execution (interrupts and I/O errors)\n- **Unlocks:** running on large or slow media without fear.\n- **Depends on:** Phase 2's journal schema and undo.\n- **Tasks (widest first):**\n  1. **Write-ahead journaling.** Write and fsync `pending`, then rename, then write `done`. Undo resolves `pending` entries by checking which name actually exists.\n  2. **A SIGINT/SIGTERM handler.** Finish the current rename, flush the journal, exit `3` and print the undo command.\n  3. **Classified I/O errors:** permission denied, read-only media, Windows file locks, disk full and long paths. Each aborts cleanly with a reason code.\n  4. **A FAT/exFAT path.** These systems have no hard links (common on SD cards). Detect them and use the exists-check + rename fallback, with the single-user race documented.\n- **Exit check:** a fault-injection suite makes the rename fail at a random Nth file, and SIGINT is sent mid-run. In every case, `undo` on the journal restores the exact original set.\n\n### Phase 4: Coverage and UX leaves\n- **Unlocks:** real-world libraries and daily use.\n- **Depends on:** Phase 3's safe executor.\n- **Tasks (widest first):**\n  1. **Companion files.** `.xmp`, `.aae` and Live Photo `.MOV` files with the same stem are renamed **as a group** with their photo, and the whole group rolls back if one rename fails. Getting this wrong breaks Lightroom and Apple Photos links.\n  2. **`--recursive`:** stays inside the root and never follows symlinks.\n  3. **Opt-in flags:** `--fallback=mtime` and `--allow-modify-date`, with every affected file flagged.\n  4. **Polish:** a progress bar (on a TTY only), a per-category summary, coloured dry-run output, and the README.\n- **Exit check:** a Lightroom- or Apple-style fixture folder keeps every photo-companion pair linked after rename and after undo. 1.0.0 is published.\n\n## 5. Cross-cutting concerns (per phase, from the first commit)\n\n| Phase | Security | Observability | Reproducibility | Resilience |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 0 | No network calls and no telemetry. Only parsed numeric date fields reach a filename; EXIF strings never do, which blocks path injection through crafted metadata. Symlinks not followed. Dependencies pinned with hashes in `uv.lock`. | JSON log line per file, summary counts, exit-code contract. CI smoke run as the canary. | `uv.lock`, a 3-OS CI matrix, a committed fixture, and builds from tags only. | Never overwrites. Stops at the first execution error and exits nonzero. A journal entry is written before the rename. |\n| 1 | Malformed and hostile EXIF fixtures. Read-byte cap and per-file timeout. All parser exceptions contained. | Reason codes for `Missing`/`Invalid`. `--explain` shows the winning tag. | A script-generated golden corpus gives the same bytes every time. Golden expected-output file. | A bad file is skipped, never fatal. Impossible dates are refused, not guessed. |\n| 2 | The resolved target path must stay inside the source directory (realpath check). The journal stores filenames only, with no GPS or other EXIF payload. | Dry-run table showing the full plan before anything changes. Collision counts. | Deterministic sort order, so identical input gives an identical plan. Seeded `hypothesis` tests. | Collision suffixing. Idempotent re-runs. `undo` command. |\n| 3 | No elevated permissions requested. Refuses to run on a filesystem root or home directory unless `--force` is given. | The journal doubles as an audit trail. The interrupt point is logged and the undo command printed. | Fault injection is deterministic: a mocked failure at the Nth rename. | Write-ahead fsync, signal handling, classified I/O errors, and the FAT fallback. |\n| 4 | Companion-file matching stays in the same directory. Recursion stays under the root. | Per-category counters (renamed, companions, skipped by reason). Progress on a TTY only, so logs stay clean when piped. | The tool version is recorded in every journal. Same version and same input give the same result. | Group-atomic companion renames with group rollback. |\n\n## 6. AI layer\n**N/A.** No model, retrieval or agent is involved. The only part of it that carries over is the data-privacy boundary, which is enforced in the gates and the Security column: metadata never leaves the machine.\n\n## 7. Deliberately deferred\n- **`--format` naming templates:** pulled forward by repeated user requests. The v1 format stays the default.\n- **Timezone conversion (`--to-utc`):** pulled forward by multi-timezone users reporting wrong order.\n- **Video files (MP4/MOV as primary files):** pulled forward by user demand. QuickTime `CreateDate` is usually **UTC**, unlike EXIF's local time, so this needs its own extraction rules and fixtures.\n- **`exiftool` backend:** pulled forward automatically if any Phase 1 fixture fails with `exifread`.\n- **Parallel EXIF reads:** pulled forward if the sync gate's throughput threshold is breached.\n- **Sorting into date folders (`YYYY/MM/`):** pulled forward by demand. Moves across directories need different collision and undo handling.\n- **Duplicate detection by content hash:** pulled forward if collision reports show many true duplicates.\n- **Standalone binaries:** pulled forward if users can't use `pipx`.\n- **Telemetry or crash reporting:** not planned. If ever added, it would be opt-in, send no metadata, and would need its own privacy review.\n- **GUI or watch-folder mode:** pulled forward only after 1.0 is stable. It would reuse `core/` as a library, per the monolith gate.\n\n## 8. Eval score: **19/20** (threshold to ship is 16 or more)\n1. **Dependency ordering, 2:** extraction is proven against a corpus before naming and collisions are specified, and the executor before companions.\n2. **Walking skeleton first, 2:** a real released wheel renames a real file on three OSes in Phase 0.\n3. **Tradeoff gates, 2:** all four standard gates plus the CLI-specific irreversible ones (name contract, timestamp source, timezone, dry-run default), each with a flip condition. AI gates marked N/A.\n4. **Blast-radius ordering, 2:** data contracts and the journal schema come before the plan builder, which comes before the dry-run UI; group atomicity comes before the progress bar.\n5. **Security threaded, 2:** a concrete move in every phase, including path injection through EXIF and staying inside the root.\n6. **Observability from day zero, 2:** logs, exit codes and the CI canary exist in Phase 0. *Limit:* there is deliberately no visibility into failures on users' machines.\n7. **Reproducibility threaded, 2:** a lockfile, a generated corpus, deterministic plans and seeded fault injection.\n8. **Resilience threaded, 2:** no overwrites from Phase 0 through group rollback in Phase 4.\n9. **AI layer, 2:** correctly declared N/A.\n10. **Deferred work, 1:** listed with pull-forward conditions, but some conditions (\"user demand\") are vague, with no threshold.\n\n**Weakest areas:** the vague deferral triggers (dimension 10), and the fact that the real-camera RAW and HEIC fixtures depend on finding sample files with clear licences.
